sections.html:
Dubuque County is where Iowa meets Illinois and Wisconsin, with the Mississippi River along its northeastern edge. Dubuque is the seat and largest city, and the 2020 count of 99,266 people made this the ninth most populous county in the state. Asbury (5,943), Dyersville (4,477), Cascade (2,386), Epworth (2,023), Peosta (1,908) and Farley (1,766) are the next largest places.

The east side is hilly Driftless country and the west is mostly rolling farmland, but a bluff house in Dubuque and a farm near Cascade are taxed and assessed through the same county offices.

The Dubuque County Treasurer collects property tax. The City of Dubuque says it does not bill or collect property taxes. The county collects them and passes the city's share along each month.

Dubuque County property tax contacts
TaskWhere to go

Mailing addressPO Box 5001, Dubuque, IA 52004-5001

Tax sale biddingOnline at iowataxauction.com

The treasurer's office takes appointments that can be booked online, which lets you skip the line. The county home page links a Beacon property records lookup. Dubuque also has a city assessor, so a parcel inside city limits may be valued by that office rather than the county's. If you are unsure, call the courthouse and give the parcel number.

Iowa's statewide calendar applies here. The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, each with a grace period through the end of the month.

  • Statements go out in August after the county auditor certifies the levy.
  • September 30 closes the first half and March 31 closes the second. If either falls on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day.
  • Unpaid first-half tax is delinquent in October and unpaid second-half tax in April.
  • Interest on a delinquent installment runs 1.5 percent per month, with a one dollar minimum.

Iowa taxes run a year behind. The September and March payments cover the fiscal year that ended the previous June 30. If you sell, you can owe tax for a period when the house was still yours even though the buyer takes over before the bill arrives.

A missing statement does not remove late charges. The owner has to make sure a bill is received and paid, and the parcel number alone is enough to pay.

Parcels with unpaid tax are sold at an online auction, usually on the third Monday of June, at iowataxauction.com. Bidders register a few days ahead. A recent county notice listed roughly 450 real estate parcels and about 130 mobile homes, with real estate amounts running from $6 to $104,077 including penalty and costs.

  • Redemption interest is 2 percent per month on the sale amount, and any part of a month counts as a full month.
  • On a regular sale, a 90-day notice of right of redemption may be issued after one year and nine months from the sale date.
  • On a public bidder sale, the 90-day notice may go out nine months after the sale.
  • A redemption only counts if the treasurer receives it before close of business on the 90th day after service is complete.

A property marked with an asterisk in the notice has been advertised for two years without a sale. If no private bid arrives, the county itself bids the amount due. Anyone holding such a parcel and thinking of selling should talk to the treasurer before the next June sale.

Iowa assessors value residential property at 100 percent of market value, and a state rollback percentage then cuts that to a taxable value. Rollbacks change every year, and statewide taxable growth for existing homes is capped at 3 percent. Real property is reassessed every two years, in odd-numbered years, and the Department of Revenue can order an adjustment if a class falls outside a 95 to 105 percent ratio band.

To contest a value, file a written protest with the local Board of Review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year. Iowa Code 441.37 allows five grounds:

  • the assessment is not equitable compared with similar property;
  • it is above the value the law allows;
  • the property is misclassified or should be exempt;
  • there is an error in the assessment;
  • there was fraud or misconduct, which must be stated specifically.

You can request a hearing in writing when you file. The board must send a written decision with its reasons. If you disagree, the next step is the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court, and the appeal board can be reached at 515-725-0338.

Slope, river flooding and age are the three physical issues buyers raise first. The city sits among bluffs, so slope matters when a buyer looks at a lot, and lower areas by the river and creeks carry flood risk. Older houses often need roofs, wiring, foundation work or sewer line repairs before a traditional buyer's inspector signs off.

A cash sale as-is avoids that repair list, though you should still confirm taxes and any special assessments with the treasurer first.

Taxes are normally prorated on the closing statement, with the buyer credited for the seller's share or the seller paying the treasurer directly. A seller closing between July 1 and December 31 owes the September installment, and a seller closing between January 1 and June 30 owes the March installment.

  • Delinquent tax and tax sale amounts must be paid in full before a clean transfer.
  • Every deed that conveys Iowa real estate for more than $500 carries state transfer tax of 80 cents per $500 or fraction above $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1).
  • A declaration of value, signed by a buyer or seller, goes to the county recorder with the deed. The recorder sends it to the assessor, who keeps it for three years.

Because the assessor receives those declarations, your sale price can become evidence in later valuation work. That is one reason to keep the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Dubuque County?
faqs.a: The Dubuque County Treasurer, at the courthouse, 720 Central Avenue in Dubuque. The City of Dubuque does not collect property tax.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the September 30 payment in Dubuque County?
faqs.a: The first half becomes delinquent in October and interest of 1.5 percent per month is added, with a one dollar minimum. If it stays unpaid, the parcel can be listed for the June tax sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dubuque County house that is on the tax sale list?
faqs.a: Yes, but the delinquent tax, penalty and costs have to be paid, usually from the sale proceeds at closing. Once a certificate is sold, redemption also carries 2 percent interest per month on the sale amount.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Dubuque County assessment?
faqs.a: Written protests go to the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year.

faqs.q: Which September or March payment does the seller owe?
faqs.a: A seller closing from July 1 to December 31 owes the September installment, and one closing from January 1 to June 30 owes the March installment.
